evidence: The FAA's Nov. 15 "Questions and Answers" page says legacy equipment became unstable when data flooded the FAA FTI network at 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds; the initial investigation points to a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris had been deploying a new router; L3Harris blocked the two locations and the network stabilized; the broadcasting function was disabled on about 60 similar routers; instability hit 17 of 22 en route centers and spread to several TRACONs; about 12,462 flights were cancelled Friday.
